pathways.title: UK track day — no race licence required
steps: Hold a valid full motorcycle road licence appropriate for the machine
Book with a recognised operator (MSV Bike Trackdays, No Limits, circuit-run days, etc.)
Bring required kit: helmet (ECE 22.06 or equivalent), leathers (1-piece or 2-piece with zip), boots, gloves. Operator kit lists vary — check before attending
Arrive early; attend compulsory rider briefing
Groups are usually novice / intermediate / advanced; declare your experience honestly
pathways.notes: No ACU competition licence needed for track days. Many riders use track days to build pace before pursuing a race licence.

pathways.title: ACU road race competition licence — Novice entry (England & Wales)
steps: Create an account on Sport80 (ACU's online portal) at sport80.com
Join an ACU-affiliated road race club (Bemsee, EMRA, No Limits Racing, NG Road Racing, etc.)
Complete the ACU Competitor Training Course (CTC) — online or in-person theory; covers regulations, flag signals and safety
Pass the Basic Rider Assessment (BRA) — on-circuit practical assessment; PDMCC Race School at Three Sisters offers combined CTC+BRA in one day (~£155)
Receive Novice (orange bib) licence and competitor number
Start racing; accumulate upgrade signatures across multiple circuits and meetings
pathways.notes: Novice intermediate grade was discontinued as of 2026 per ACU standing regulations update.

pathways.title: ACU licence upgrade — Novice to Clubman
steps: Compete as a Novice at ACU-permitted meetings and collect upgrade signatures from Clerk of Course
Signatures required at a minimum of 3 different circuits (verify current count in ACU Standing Regulations — requirements change year to year)
After required signatures, apply for Clubman grade via Sport80
Clubman licence removes orange novice bib restriction and opens more class entries
pathways.notes: Upgrade signature counts and requirements are set annually in the ACU Standing Regulations. Always check the current-year handbook PDF from acu.org.uk.

pathways.title: ACU licence upgrade — Clubman to National
steps: Race as Clubman and collect National upgrade signatures across permitted events
Apply for National licence via Sport80; medical declaration required
National licence allows entry to national championships including BSB support classes where eligible

pathways.title: SACU licence pathway (Scotland)
steps: Contact SACU or a SACU-affiliated club; main short-circuit venue is Knockhill
Complete SACU training and any medical requirements
Arrange start permission (inter-association) when competing at ACU England/Wales events

pathways.title: MCUI pathway (Northern Ireland — short circuit)
steps: Contact MCUI Ulster Centre or a local affiliated club
Complete MCUI licence and medical requirements
Primary venues: Bishopscourt Racing Circuit and Kirkistown Racing Circuit
Arrange inter-association permission for ACU (GB) events

pathways.title: Isle of Man / public-road event licence (TT / Manx GP / NW200)
steps: Hold an ACU National or International licence (or equivalent FIM-affiliate licence)
Submit entry to ACM / event organisers well before closing date — events are heavily oversubscribed
For Manx Grand Prix (entry level): no prior TT experience required; qualification lap requirements apply
For Isle of Man TT: prior Manx GP or equivalent road-race experience required; qualification laps mandatory
For North West 200: MCUI or ACU licence plus race history submitted to organisers
Specialist public-road insurance and supplementary regulations apply — these are separate from short-circuit events
pathways.notes: Public-road events carry significantly higher risk. Competitors must understand and accept full supplementary regulations. Separate medical and safety briefings mandatory.
